newsitem.title: INDIA: Weizman proposes India-Israel air force ties.
newsitem.headline: Weizman proposes India-Israel air force ties.

text.p: Visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman said on Thursday his country would open an air force liaison office in New Delhi to boost ties with its Indian counterpart, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported.
It quoted Weizman, visiting a southern Indian air base, as saying the two countries had many things in common in aviation.
India's first visit by an Israeli head of state triggered worries in neighbouring Pakistan, New Delhi's traditional foe which has refused to establish ties with the Jewish state.
A Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesman in Islamabad said South Asian countries were concerned by what he called growing cooperation between India and Israel, particularly in the military field.

"Both (countries) are nuclear or known nuclear states with tested ballistic missile capability and both states have a long history of uneasy relations with their neighbours," he said, referring to prolonged hostility between India and Pakistan and between Israel and its Arab neighbours.

"Naturally, the growing cooperation between these two countries, particularly in the...military-related fields, would be a cause of concern to the countries of South Asia," the spokesman said without elaborating on such cooperation. "So we are keeping the situation under review."
Indian newspapers have quoted Weizman as offering Israeli Kfir fighter planes to New Delhi during his visit which began on Sunday.
However, an Israeli official told Reuters that India was not interested in the Kfirs, saying they were too old for the Indian Air Force.
PTI quoted the visiting head of Israeli Aicraft Industries, Keret Moshe, as saying he expected major purchases by India in the fields of aeronautics and high-end electronics.

"We are here to offer whatever we can from our capabilities to India, and it is on the part of Indians to take advantage of it," Moshe said in the southern city of Bangalore where he was accompanying Weizman.
PTI quoted Moshe as offering Israel's EL/M 2022-A maritime surveillance radar to the Indian Navy to counter Pakistan's Orion radar.
"The discussions are in progress and I cannot disclose anything further at the moment," Moshe said.
PTI said India had signed a $10 million contract in December for the purchase of Israel's Super Dvora multi-mission patrol boats. Indian officials declined to comment.

The Indian media focused on Weizman's talks on "terrorism" earlier in the week with Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, a term usually used by New Delhi to describe separatist militants in its border states.
But Weizman told Reuters on Tuesday that he had discussed terrorism in its global context and in a general way.
Pakistan denies Indian charges it trains and arms Kashmir's separatist militants but says Islambad gives them diplomatic support.
Weizman told India's Doordarshan television of his meeting with then Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto at the inaugural ceremony of South African President Nelson Mandela.
"I was introduced to her. She didn't run away from me," Weizman said. "But when I invited her to visit Israel she said it was too early. She is a charming lady."
